videos.title: Jang Dong-hyeok: “(The ruling party’s) Starbucks boycott will only last until June 3rd... The tar...
videos.subtitle_summary:
1. Jang Dong-hyeok predicts that the Starbucks boycott by the ruling party will last until June 3rd, suggesting they will return to Starbucks coffee after that date. He recalls the opposition party's strong stance against Samsung in 2016, which quickly faded after the election.
2. The speaker suggests that Park Geun-hye's impeachment trial and special investigation anger has been redirected towards Starbucks in this election, making it the main target. He criticizes Song Young-gil, a prominent figure in the opposition party, for his past actions related to the 5.18 Democratization Movement.
3. The speaker calls for the public to judge between Song Young-gil and Starbucks, implying that they should hold both accountable. He concludes by urging voters to show their support for freedom and democracy by choosing their own coffee on this Friday (the day of the election).

videos.title: Starbucks 'Tank Day' event sparks political battle… Lee's criticism met with "election-geared ant...
videos.subtitle_summary: Starbucks 'Tank Day' event has sparked a political controversy. Lee criticized the event due to its marketing phrase, which reminded him of the Sewol Ferry disaster. The event took place on April 18th and Lee accused Starbucks of intentionally using the date for their promotion, implying insensitivity towards the tragedy. This has been perceived as inappropriate behavior by some, and calls have been made to review and possibly shut down the site associated with the event.
